summary: Tested the Clerk auth-config fix (placeholder-key detection plus proxy_url resolved against the backend URL). Backend: 9 new tests in test_clerk_config.py; the full suite passes (39/39). Frontend: the invalid_keys message works with a mocked config. With the page served from a fake separate origin, the relative proxy_url resolves to REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Admin and employee ticket sign-in and reload still work.
critical_code_review_comments: Optional: if clerk-js fails to load (e.g. a misconfigured proxy or a blocked CDN), Clerk raises an unhandled rejection (failed_to_load_clerk_js) and the sign-in screen is left without a form. Consider catching it and showing a friendly message, the same way the invalid_keys case does.

Optional: when config returns enabled:false with no reason (keys empty), the frontend retries 20 times x 1.5s (~30s) before showing 'unavailable'. The backend could return reason:'missing_keys' so the frontend can show the config message right away.
Optional: the sk regex [A-Za-z0-9]{20,} is stricter than the pk regex. Today's Clerk secret keys are alphanumeric, so this is fine, but it would reject a key format containing '_' or '-'.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_clerk_config.py runs clerk_auth.clerk_config() in a subprocess with a CLERK_* env override (does not touch .env). The frontend proxy URL check served the app from the fake origin https://erms-fake-frontend.test via page.route, forwarding to preview, and mocked /api/clerk/config. Tickets come from tests/clerk_test_users.py --tokens.
